correctness.rationale: For m,n>=2, graph balls have radii zero, one and two. On K_mn the centered maximal values are max{x_u,(x_u+Y)/(n+1),mu} on A and max{y_v,(y_v+X)/(m+1),mu} on B. For a cut of k occupied A and ell occupied B, the input edge variation is D=k(n-ell)+(m-k)ell; the two possible strict above-global-mean values for unoccupied vertices cannot coexist because they would require incompatible inequalities. Case analysis bounds the output cut variation by max(R_A,R_B), with equality at a singleton spike in the maximizing class, R_A=m/(m+1)+(m-1)(n-1)/((m+1)(m+n)) and R_B its swapped formula. For all nonzero real f supported only on A, the normalized values p_u and chord majorization of g(s)=|max{s,1/(m+n)}-1/(m+1)| give sum g(p_u)<=R_A, with strict inequality for every non-spike and pointwise deficit at least kappa_A min{s,1-s}. Summing proves the stated rigidity. Algebra gives R_A-1=((m-2)(n-2)-3)/((m+1)(m+n)) and its B swap, hence the exact threshold and limit sup2. Independent Fraction enumeration checked every cut class for 2<=m,n<=9 and the threshold identity. These do not prove all m,n or all real one-sided profiles, which follow from the symbolic case split and chord inequality.
